paragraphs: Baker, here's what I want you to take home from this one. Israel looked across the Jordan, saw a big altar, and went straight to war talk. The whole congregation assembled at Shiloh to go to war (Joshua 22:12). But they did the wise thing next: they sent Phinehas and ten chiefs to ask first (Joshua 22:13-14).

Now watch what the asking uncovered. The three tribes weren't turning from the LORD at all. They built that altar because they were afraid their descendants might one day hear, "You have no share in the LORD!" (Joshua 22:25). They wanted a witness that they belong to Him too. Friend, I have SEEN what a wrong guess does to a good heart, and I sat in a drawer for years guessing wrong about my own story. So before you decide what someone means, go and listen.

And listen to how it ended. Phinehas and the chiefs heard every word and were satisfied (Joshua 22:30). Israel blessed God and spoke no more about war (Joshua 22:33). Zeal for the LORD is a good thing, but it needs patience and good questions, because love for Him can look strange from across a river. Ask first, listen well, and you might find a brother where you expected a fight.
